newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Poll gives Democrat Party a 10-seat lead in upcoming elections. The Democrat Party is projected to win 132 seats in the elections on Sunday, outpacing its main rival New Aspiration Party (NAP) by 10 seats, according to a national poll by The Nation newspaper. The poll shows the NAP will win 122 seats, Chart Pattana, 51, Chart Thai, 36 and Social Action 20. The poll surveyed 71,057 likely voters, of whom 8,463 were from Bankok, from Nov 4 to 11. (THE NATION)

- The attoney-general's decision to drop the Phuket land reform case against 15 wealthy recipients is illegal, the deputy police director-general said. Police General Salang Nunnag said legislation should be enacted to serve as a check and balance mechanism on the attorney-general's power. The officer made his remarks while explaining to the cabinet how the police handled cases involving the cabinet of former prime minister Chuan Leekpai, three land reform officials and 15 Phuket residents granted land under the reform scheme. (BANGKOK POST).
- Election watchdog PollWatch submitted evidence to the national police chief that four New Aspiration Party cabinet members and another NAP candidate had violated the election law. (THE NATION)

- TelecomAsia benefits from service revamp. TelecomAsia Corp will benefit from major changes, including a new charging system for local calls, approved for Thailand's telephone service. The Telephone Organisation of Thailand's board of directors agreed in principle to the changes that will take effect when working committees have completed fine details. Calls will be charged on time and distance instead of current flat rate of three baht per call. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thai-U.S. tax treaty ready for Clinton. Thailand and the United States have endorsed the draft of the double taxation avoidance treaty which is like to be enforced from 1998, the Finance Ministry said. Finance Minister Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said the treaty will be signed by Prime Minister Banhanrn Silpa-archa and U.S. President Bill Clinton during the American president's visit to Bangkok later this month. (THE NATION)

- Unocal Thailand announced an increase of petroleum reserves in the Gulf of Thailand of more than 300 million cubic feet with the discovery of a new gas field, extensions to its existing three gas fields, and the proving of the commercial value of two other gas fields. (THE NATION)
